title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Fix a type (g,ν). Let X_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} → Spec Q be the universal curve over the moduli stack. Let M_{g,ν} = π1 of the universal curve and N_{g,ν} = π1 of the moduli stack (both profinite, over Q). They sit in the diagram (1_{g,ν}): 1 → Ŝ_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} → 1 and 1 → T̂_{g,ν} → N_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} → 1. Here T̂ is the profinite Teichmüller modular group, Ŝ the geometric π1 of the universal curve, and π̂_{g,ν} = ker(M → N) the profinite surface group.

A curve with marked point (X,x) of type (g,ν) over a field k of characteristic 0 is a k-point of the universal curve. Its étale path torsor P_{X,x} is a right M_{g,ν}-torsor. It is in fact a bitorsor, with the twisted group M_{X,x} acting on the left. Every invariant of (X,x) is obtained from it by contracted products, formula (4): π_{X,x}, S_{X,x}, T_{X,x}, M_{X,x}, N_X, and the algebraic closure Q̃ of Q in k.

This page.
- (5) defines the pushed-forward torsors. Q_X = P_{X,x} ∧^{M} N is an N-torsor (paths on the moduli stack to ξ). R = P_{X,x} ∧^{M} Γ ≃ Q_X ∧^{N} Γ is a Γ_Q-torsor, essentially Isom(Q̄, Q̃).
- So Q̃ and the whole diagram (1) for (X,x) are determined by the M_{g,ν}-torsor (3).
- Converse fails over algebraic fields. If k is algebraic over Q (k = Q̃, or k = Q̄ with R trivialized), P_{X,x} cannot recover X over k.
- The argument is by cardinality of automorphisms. Aut(P_{X,x}) = M_{X,x}. Once R is trivialized, P reduces its structure group to the geometric kernel; the automorphisms of the reduced torsor form the geometric group (S_{X,x}), of continuum cardinality. By contrast, automorphisms of (X,x) inducing the identity on k = Q̃ (identified with Q̄) form a finite group, since the curve is hyperbolic.
- So the functor (points) → (torsors) is far from fully faithful over algebraic fields.
- 'Mais...': (6) writes k = lim K_i over subfields of finite type. The structure (X,x) descends to some K_i, which the next page develops.

The page serves the 'Teichmüller tower' programme: realize points of M_{g,ν} and of the universal curve as Galois-theoretic data (sections or torsors). It is the motivation for why the anabelian/section statement for the moduli stack must be posed over fields of finite type rather than over Q̄.
errors: No real mathematical error. The automorphism-cardinality argument proves only non-faithfulness. The stronger fact is that over Q̄ all such torsors are isomorphic to one another (the torsor carries no information); this is not stated but is implicit.

Notational inconsistency: Q_x in (5) should be Q_X, consistent with (4). The reduced structure group is written with a symbol resembling T̂ / 𝒯̂; by the logic (trivializing R reduces an M-torsor to ker(M→Γ)), it should be Ŝ_{g,ν}, with automorphisms in S_{X,x}.

ideas.what: Points of the universal curve / moduli stack over k give path torsors (bitorsors) under π1 of the stack, from which all fundamental-group data of (X,x) are obtained by contracted product
ideas.modern_name: étale path torsor / twisting of the Teichmüller tower by a rational point; Galois sections of π1(M_{g,ν,K}) → Γ_K
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in general form

ideas.what: Over algebraic (or algebraically closed) fields the torsor cannot recover the point: Aut(torsor) is uncountable while Aut(X,x) is finite; hence one must work over fields of finite type, writing k as a direct limit of such fields
ideas.modern_name: necessity of finitely generated base fields in anabelian / section conjectures (here for M_{g,ν})
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (anabelian conjecture over fields of finite type; M_{g,ν} listed among anabelian objects)

missed.claim: Explicit early (1981-82) formulation of the moduli-stack version of the anabelian programme. Points of the universal curve over K are to be recovered from π1-torsors under M_{g,ν}, with the explicit cardinality argument for why algebraic base fields fail. This predates the Faltings letter, but the idea itself is known from that letter.
missed.quote: la donnée de P_{X,x} ne suffit pas pour récupérer X sur k — p.ex. les autom. des torseurs P_{X,x} sont les éléments de M_{X,x} — ils ont la puissance du continu
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The section conjecture for moduli stacks M_{g,ν} remains largely open. This shows Grothendieck envisaged it in this torsor form early on. Historically interesting, but not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean heuristic motivating finitely-generated base fields for an anabelian statement about M_{g,ν}. It is consistent with and anticipates the Faltings letter / Esquisse, but contains no result absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais bien mieux [?]' is more plausibly 'Mais bien sûr'.
'i.e. ou [?] R trivialisé' is likely 'i.e. avec R trivialisé'.
'sous-corps de t.f.' = sous-corps de type fini.
The 'T̂_{g,ν}-torseurs' / 'élément de T̂_{X,x}' symbols appear to be fraktur Ŝ_{g,ν} / S_{X,x}, the geometric kernel, by the logic of the argument.
'k = Q̃ (donné ≃ Q̂)' should be '(≃ Q̄ donné)'.
